subject: Negative Marginal log-Likelihood- how to improve model?

messages.author: 21eb6088fd687103
messages.subject: Negative Marginal log-Likelihood- how to improve model?
parts:
Hello everyone, 

I am not sure if this is an appropriate question to ask here as I am quite new to the using Bayesian framework, so I apologize if this is below intended the level of discussion here. 

But I am trying to use INLA-SPDE to predict functional richness (a continuous variable with a normal distribution) across a landscape. I have gotten the code to run with a simple formula where: functional richness ~ elevation + f(spatial, model=spde), using family = 'gaussian', and all other settings on default. The code runs fine and the credible intervals for the intercept, elevation, and spatial component all look good (not crossing 0). However, the Marginal log-likelihood is negative and 'failure' is coming back as NA after about 480 iterations (before this is 0). I am wondering if anyone has advice or resources to help me with the next steps to adjust the model and hopefully create a valid model. 

Thank you!
Katie

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Negative Marginal log-Likelihood- how to improve model?
parts:
For continuous density models like the Gaussian, a negative marginal log-likelihood can be entirely normal (pun not intended), as the logarithm of a density can be negative. (And for discrete models it will always be negative since probabilities are at most 1). So it’s not clear to me what the (perceived) problem is; what is becoming a “failure”, and what is iterating 480 times?
Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Negative Marginal log-Likelihood- how to improve model?
parts:
Hi Finn, 

Thank you for your quick response! Sorry let me clarify-- I read that one way to assess model convergence is to look at the CPO, and that if failure is reported as 0 it indicates that all Laplace approximations were successful, and if failure is reported as "NA" there may be problems with the model convergence. I used the line of code below, and the first ~480 records were reported as 0, and then after that were all NAs
> model[["cpo"]][["failure"]]" 

-Katie
